verification_report.summary: The proof is correct. The CLD star topology makes the U_n nested and prevents their intersection from containing a centre-neighbourhood. The branchwise construction satisfies the exact CLD smoothness requirements: the profiles agree at the centre, only two are nonconstant, full profiles are constant near −infinity, and the centre slopes 1 and −1 balance. Nonnegative branch second derivatives give smooth psh functions. Any common representative neighbourhood has only finitely many exceptional branches, so some b_n is full; there smoothness forces derivative 0 near −infinity while convexity makes the derivative nondecreasing, contradicting the germ-imposed centre derivative −1. The scaling construction is positive, decreasing to zero, and its k=1 representatives would recover common representatives of the f_n after multiplication by 2 and subtraction of a constant. The conclusions about row limits, the global zero function, and the limited scope of the example follow. The cited CLD definitions and criteria were checked against the [primary arXiv text](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.6277) and match the proof's usage.
